kept.q: Which of the following best defines a projectile in Physics?
options: An object that moves in a straight line at constant speed under no external force
An object that is given an initial velocity and thereafter moves only under the action of gravity
An object that moves along a circular path with a constant centripetal force
An object that remains stationary while subjected to gravitational force
kept.explanation: A projectile is any object launched into the air that is then acted upon only by gravity (ignoring air resistance). It follows a curved path called a trajectory.
kept.pidgin: Projectile na any object wey dem throw go air, after that na only gravity dey work on am (we no dey count air resistance). E dey follow curve path wey dem call trajectory.

kept.q: Chidi throws a stone horizontally from the top of a cliff that is 45 m high, with an initial speed of 20 m/s. Taking g = 10 m/s^2, calculate the time it takes the stone to reach the ground.
kept.explanation: For horizontal projection, vertical motion only depends on height and gravity: h = (1/2)g t^2. So 45 = (1/2)(10)t^2, giving t^2 = 9, t = 3.0 s. The horizontal speed does not affect the time of fall.
kept.pidgin: For horizontal throw, na only height and gravity dey control how e take fall: h = (1/2)g t^2. So 45 = (1/2)(10)t^2, t^2 = 9, t = 3.0 s. The horizontal speed no dey change the time wey e go take land.

kept.q: A ball is projected from level ground with an initial velocity of 20 m/s at an angle of 45° to the horizontal. Taking g = 10 m/s^2, calculate the horizontal range of the ball.
kept.explanation: Range formula: R = u^2 sin(2theta)/g = (20^2)(sin90)/10 = 400(1)/10 = 40 m. At 45°, sin(2theta)=sin90=1, giving maximum range for that speed.
kept.pidgin: Range formula na R = u^2 sin(2theta)/g = (20^2)(sin90)/10 = 400(1)/10 = 40 m. Since e be 45°, sin(2theta) = sin90 = 1, so the range reach im maximum for that speed.

kept.q: A car of mass 800 kg moves round a circular track of radius 50 m at a constant speed of 10 m/s. Calculate the centripetal force acting on the car.
kept.explanation: Centripetal force F = mv^2/r = (800 x 10^2)/50 = 800 x 100/50 = 1600 N. This force is directed towards the centre of the circular path and is provided by friction between the tyres and the road.
kept.pidgin: Centripetal force na F = mv^2/r = (800 x 10^2)/50 = 800 x 100/50 = 1600 N. Na dis force dey point go centre of the circle, and na friction between tyre and road dey provide am.

kept.q: A stone is projected with a speed of 30 m/s at an angle of 60° to the horizontal. Taking g = 10 m/s^2, calculate the maximum height reached by the stone.
kept.explanation: Maximum height H = u^2 sin^2(theta)/(2g) = (30^2)(sin60)^2/20 = 900 x 0.75/20 = 33.75 m. Only the vertical component of the velocity (u sin theta) is used for the height calculation.
kept.pidgin: Maximum height na H = u^2 sin^2(theta)/(2g) = (30^2)(sin60)^2/20 = 900 x 0.75/20 = 33.75 m. Na only the up-down part of the speed (u sin theta) dem dey use calculate the height.

kept.q: A bucket containing water is whirled in a vertical circle of radius 1.0 m. Taking g = 10 m/s^2, calculate the minimum speed of the bucket at the topmost point of the circle so that the water does not spill out.
kept.explanation: At the top of the circle, for water not to spill, the weight of the water must supply just enough centripetal force: mg = mv^2/r, so v = sqrt(gr) = sqrt(10 x 1.0) = sqrt(10) = 3.16 m/s. Below this speed, gravity would be more than needed, and the water would fall out before completing the loop.
kept.pidgin: For top of the circle, make water no comot, the weight of water must jus provide the centripetal force wey e need: mg = mv^2/r, so v = sqrt(gr) = sqrt(10 x 1.0) = sqrt(10) = 3.16 m/s. If speed too small pass dis, gravity go pull the water comot before e complete the loop.
